senses.gloss: लोप m. breaking, hurting, injury, destruction, interruption, MBh.; Kāv. &c.
neglect, violation, transgression (of a vow or duty), Mn.; Yājñ. &c.
robbing, plundering, MBh.
want, deficiency, absence, disappearance, ŚrS.; Ragh.

(in gram.) dropping, elision (generally as distinguished from the terms लुप्, श्लु, लुक्, which are only applicable to affixes; when लोप of an affix takes place, a blank is substituted, which exerts the same influence on the base as the affix itself, but when either लुक् or लुप् or श्लु of an affix is enjoined, then the affix is not only dropped but it is also inoperative on the base; thus in the 1st pl. of कति, where जस् is said to be elided by लुक्, the change of the final of the base to Guṇa does not take place i.e. both the affix and its effect on the base are abolished; moreover, लोप refers only to the last letter of an affix, whereas by लुक् &c. the dropping of the whole affix is implied), Nir.; Prāt.; Pāṇ. &c.
लोप लोपक &c. See p. 904, col. 3.
लो॑पा f. a partic. bird, TS.
a kind of bird, L.
= लोपा-मुद्रा below.
लोपापत्ति f. the being cut off or dropped or elided, MW.
लोपक mfn. (ifc.) interrupting, violating, destroying (see विधि-ल्˚)
लोपक m. violation, MW.
लोपाक m. a kind of jackal, Suśr.
लोपिका f. a kind of sweetmeat, AgP.; Hcat.
लोपन n. the act of omitting or violating, violation (see व्रत-ल्˚)
the mouth, Gal. (prob. w.r. for लपन).
लोपापक m. id. (f(इका). ), L.

लोपा-मुद्रा f. N. of the reputed wife of the sage Agastya (she is said to have been formed by the sage himself and then secretly introduced into the palace of the king of Vidarbha, where she grew up as his daughter; she asked her husband to acquire immense riches; so he went to the rich demon Ilvala, and having conquered him, satisfied his wife with his wealth; she is considered as the authoress of RV. i, 179, 4), RV.; MBh.; Hariv. &c.
लोपा-मुद्रा—कवि m. N. of a poet, Cat.
लोपा-मुद्रा—पति m. husband of Lopā-mudrā, N. of Agastya, L.
लोपा-मुद्रा—सहचर m. husband of Lopā-mudrā, N. of Agastya, L.
लोपायिका f. a kind of bird, L.
लोपाश॑ m. a jackal, fox, or a similar animal, RV.; VS. [cf. Gk. ἀλώπηξ]
लोपा˚शक m. N. of a man, Buddh.
लोपा˚शिका f. a female jackal or fox, L.
लोपिन् mfn. (ifc.) injuring, diminishing, impairing, MBh.; Ragh.
liable or subject to elision, Pat., (cf. मध्यम-पद-त्˚).
लोप्तृ mfn. one who interrupts or violates (with gen.), MBh.
लोप्त्री (त्री), f. a lump of dough or paste, Bhpr.
लोप्त्र n. stolen property, plunder, booty, Yājñ.; MBh.
लोप्य mfn. to be broken &c.
to be omitted or elided, Vop.
being among thickets or inaccessible places, VS. (Mahīdh.)
